history.content: when did the first chucky movie come out
The first Chucky movie, titled "Child's Play," was released on November 9, 1988.

The film series originally started as straightforward horror with the first installment, "Child's Play," which contains more psychological horror elements. However, its successors evolved into typical slasher films infused with dark humor. As the series progressed, it became increasingly satirical and campy, eventually transitioning briefly into horror comedy. 
The story revolves around a serial killer and voodoo practitioner named Charles Lee "Chucky" Ray, who transfers his soul into a child-sized "Good Guy" doll through a voodoo ritual after being mortally wounded. The doll is later found by a homeless peddler and sold to Karen Barclay, who gives it to her son, Andy, as a birthday gift. 
Chucky must possess the first person he revealed his secret to—Andy—in order to restore his soul and escape from the doll's body. He terrorizes the Barclays in an attempt to accomplish this before his soul becomes permanently trapped in the doll.
How many movies are in the series?

There are eight movies in the Child's Play series, with the possibility of more to come. The films include "Child's Play" (1988), "Child's Play 2" (1990), "Child's Play 3" (1991), "Bride of Chucky" (1998), "Seed of Chucky" (2004), "Curse of Chucky" (2013), "Cult of Chucky" (2017), and "Child's Play" (2019).
Additionally, there are plans for a TV series called "Chucky," which will continue the story of the films.
Yes. In February 2018, it was announced that a television series titled "Child's Play: The TV Series" is in development, with franchise creator Don Mancini and producer David Kirschner involved.
I heard that they have released a video game as well. Is that true?

Slimstown Studios has announced the release of an endless runner video game titled "Chucky: Slash & Dash." The game will be available on iPhone, iPad, iPod Touch, and Android devices. In "Child's Play," players will join Chucky, trapped in a never-ending nightmare, endlessly running through the factory producing Good Guys dolls.
Wow! It is a very profitable franchise.
I am sorry that I am not sure if this will be very profitable franchise.
Are there any negative consequences? After all, it is a very violent story.

Yes. In December 1992, four individuals who tortured and killed 16-year-old Suzanne Capper were reported to be influenced by one of the "Child's Play" movies. During the torture, the perpetrators taunted the girl by playing her a song titled "Hi, I'm Chucky (Wanna Play?)" by 150 Volts, which features samples from the film. Additionally, in 1993, two youths who abducted and murdered a toddler named James Bulger were said to have been influenced by "Child's Play 3."
